assumptions: The monitor, chamber glass, and observation slit can be arranged so no composition independently proves whether the anomalous reflection is real.
The planet image can remain absent from the slit until the scripted rotation reveal.
Final wardrobe, production-surface colors, and camera-to-set clearances are not yet confirmed; palette and lens descriptions therefore specify relationships rather than equipment or exact finishes.
aspect_ratio: 2.00:1, using the horizontal span to hold Ninel, monitor, and observation slit in meaningful separation while the compact set remains compressed rather than expansive.
point_of_view: Remain inside Ninel's incomplete access to the bay: the frame may observe her from nearby but may not reveal the monitor anomaly, Argo's intent, or the concealed planet independently of what she can register. Preserve uncertainty over whether the reflection is perceptual, system-generated, or real.
palette: near-black graphite for inactive ship surfaces and the monitor
cold blue-green in chamber glass, frost, and the eventual planet
restrained emergency red as a periodic system intrusion
low-saturation skin and neutral fabric tones that do not pre-label Ninel as human or machine
contrast: Keep the bay's deepest surfaces distinct enough to retain geometry, while Ninel's face and hands emerge through narrow value separation rather than glossy isolation. Let the monitor read as a near-black plane until it carries the disputed image, and reserve the largest color-and-value separation for the blue-green planet at the final turn.
texture: Favor clean, controlled image rendering with hard-edged architecture; allow tactile irregularity only in frost, condensation, skin, and the planet. Preserve restrained highlight roll-off on glass and the monitor so reflections remain legible without becoming supernatural spectacle.
lens_strategy: Begin with a restricted field of view and close camera-to-subject relationship that withholds complete bay geography, using full-frame-equivalent moderate-to-short-telephoto behavior indicatively and avoiding conspicuous facial distortion. Move toward a restrained normal-to-moderate-wide field of view only as Ninel acts and spatial relationships become dramatically necessary; maintain sufficient depth coherence at the final reveal for Ninel and the slit to share the frame without implying that the camera knows more than she does.
visual_motifs: sealed rectangles within rectangles: chamber glass, black monitor, and observation slit
paired images that almost agree: body and reflection, frost movement and chosen breath, Ninel and the world behind her
empty horizontal space withheld beside Ninel, then claimed by the planet at Argo's final answer
prohibited_defaults: independent inserts or privileged angles that verify the reflection after Ninel turns away
unmotivated handheld instability or horror-coded canted framing
extreme wide-angle proximity that caricatures Ninel or the compact architecture
premature views of the full bay or observation slit that spend the final reveal early
generic centered symmetry used after Ninel begins testing the room
decorative shallow focus that obscures the frost, monitor-body disagreement, or planet relationship required by the beat
exceptions: Break the initial sealed central geometry when Ninel deliberately forces her first breath at S01-B01; her self-directed act earns the first meaningful imbalance and additional surrounding space.
Allow body and reflection to occupy competing visual centers only during the disputed monitor moment in S01-B02; return to Ninel's accessible evidence as soon as the monitor clears.

Use the scene's widest shared geography only when the planet enters the slit during Argo's pause and answer in S01-B03; the expansion is permitted because the new world makes the withheld past more threatening, not because the location needs exposition.
Permit the blue-green planet to exceed the established palette's restraint only at the word 'failure' in S01-B03, making discovery and danger arrive as one value turn.

rules.composition: Contain Ninel inside the chamber's rectilinear boundaries with fragments of face, frost, glass, and diagnostic surfaces carrying more of the frame than readable room geography. Before the breath, keep her body aligned with the chamber's imposed axis and deny her usable open space.
rules.camera_height: Hold near chamber-bed height, level with Ninel's resting face and the frost above it; do not look down on her as a specimen or raise the camera before she initiates action.
rules.dramatic_purpose: Make consciousness feel like incomplete sensory assembly and establish the room's geometry as an instruction Ninel has not yet chosen to resist.

rules.composition: When Ninel chooses to breathe, introduce a small asymmetry and enough adjacent space for the visible breath and moving frost to form a cause-and-response pair; preserve the chamber frame so agency registers as a change within constraint, not freedom from it.
rules.camera_height: Remain at her eye-line as she becomes active, allowing height to follow her only when she sits rather than anticipating the rise.
rules.dramatic_purpose: Mark the first breath as a deliberate experiment and the scene's first self-directed visual change.

rules.composition: Frame Ninel and the black monitor as two adjacent image planes, with neither granted an objective master view. During the disagreement, keep both readable just long enough for their eyelines to conflict; after she turns, do not isolate the monitor in a composition that supplies evidence unavailable to her.
rules.camera_height: Use Ninel's newly seated eye-line and keep the monitor encounter level; avoid a low or high angle that declares either image dominant or true.
rules.dramatic_purpose: Convert curiosity into distrust while preserving the anomaly as unconfirmed rather than presenting it as an external supernatural fact.

rules.composition: During Ninel's question and Argo's pause, place her off the chamber's original axis and hold the observation-slit side as dark negative space. When the planet appears, let it occupy that withheld space in the same frame relationship as Ninel, with the slit still visibly containing it rather than turning the world into an unrestricted vista.
rules.camera_height: Stay at Ninel's seated or standing eye-line, level enough to bind her and the slit to one uncertain present; do not elevate into an explanatory overview when the planet arrives.
rules.dramatic_purpose: Make Argo's withheld history become an external threat at the exact moment the world enlarges the mystery, while keeping Ninel rather than the spectacle as the viewer's anchor.
